\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{هدر} \fa{دادن} (hadar dâdan)}{هدر دادن (hadar dâdan)}]{\fa{هدر} \fa{دادن} (hadar dâdan) — to waste}

\label{lesson:FA-C149-hadar-dadan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to get a flat tyre, then the Persian for to get stuck.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{هدر} \fa{دادن}}
\textbf{\fa{هدر} \fa{دادن}} — \emph{hadar dâdan} — \textquotedblleft{}to waste\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{hadar dâdan} pairs \emph{hadar}, borrowed from Arabic \emph{hadar}, \textquotedblleft{}something lost in vain\textquotedblright{} (root \emph{h-d-r}, Lane), with the Persian verb \emph{dâdan}, \textquotedblleft{}to give\textquotedblright{}. \emph{dâdan}, \textquotedblleft{}to give\textquotedblright{}, is an inherited verb; EtymDB takes it back to the Indo-European root \emph{*deh\textsubscript{3}-}, \textquotedblleft{}to give\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{صرفه} \fa{جویی} \fa{کردن} (sarfejuyi kardan)}{صرفه جویی کردن (sarfejuyi kardan)}]{\fa{صرفه} \fa{جویی} \fa{کردن} (sarfejuyi kardan) — to economise}

\label{lesson:FA-C149-sarfejuyi-kardan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to get stuck, then the Persian for to waste.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{صرفه} \fa{جویی} \fa{کردن}}
\textbf{\fa{صرفه} \fa{جویی} \fa{کردن}} — \emph{sarfejuyi kardan} — \textquotedblleft{}to economise\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{sarfejuyi kardan} pairs \emph{sarfejuyi}, \textquotedblleft{}thrift\textquotedblright{}, with \emph{kardan}. It is \emph{sarfe}, \textquotedblleft{}saving, profit\textquotedblright{}, with \emph{-ju}, \textquotedblleft{}seeking\textquotedblright{}, and \emph{-i}. \emph{sarfe} is usually traced to Arabic \emph{ṣarf}, \textquotedblleft{}spending, turning\textquotedblright{} (root \emph{ṣ-r-f}, Lane); \emph{-ju} is native. \emph{kardan}, \textquotedblleft{}to do\textquotedblright{}, is an inherited verb, from Middle Persian \emph{kardan} (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}
